h1: The 6 Best Food Processors Under $500 of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Food Processors Under $500: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: six food processors under $500, compared on bowl size, motor, discs and build to match your kitchen and cooking habits.
summary: The Breville BFP810 Sous Chef 16 Cup is the best overall food processor under $500 for big batches. The Cuisinart DFP-14BCNY is the best value for most kitchens, and the Breville BFP610 suits smaller cooking. The Cuisinart Pro Custom 11-Cup is the easy-clean pick.
intro: A bigger bowl does not make a better food processor, and that is the most common mistake at this price. A 16-cup bowl sounds like a bargain until you realize you will be washing and storing it for two cups of salsa, so the right size depends on how you actually cook.

We reviewed eight machines in the $200 to $500 range and ranked six on their spec sheets: bowl capacity, motor, included discs, build material and cleanup. The Ninja BlendSense is a blender system rather than a true processor, so we left it out.

products.name: Breville BFP810 Sous Chef 16 Cup Food Processor
products.verdict: The 16-cup bowl is the largest here, wrapped in brushed stainless Sous Chef build.
products.description:
The Breville BFP810 Sous Chef has a 16-cup bowl, the largest in this group, and brushed stainless steel construction from the Sous Chef line. For batch cooking, shredding cabbage for a crowd or making dough in volume, it removes the need to work in rounds.

It ranks above the Cuisinart 14-cup models because the extra capacity and metal build are the more premium combination, even though the Cuisinarts cost less to store and match it on core tasks. You pay for the room and the finish.

Buy it if you cook for a family or meal-prep weekly. The caveat is counter and cabinet space: a 16-cup machine is a commitment, and small kitchens will resent it.
products.idealFor: Families and meal-preppers who cook big batches.
products.skipIf: You cook for one or two and have limited storage.

products.name: Cuisinart Food Processor, 14-Cup, DFP-14BCNY, 720W
products.verdict: A 14-cup bowl and 720-watt motor handle chopping, shredding and dough for less.
products.description:
The Cuisinart DFP-14BCNY pairs a 14-cup work bowl with a 720-watt motor and covers mincing, dicing, shredding, pureeing and dough. That is nearly the same task list as machines costing more.

It sits behind the Breville BFP810 because the bowl is two cups smaller and the build is less premium. In exchange you get the same family of jobs at a friendlier price, which is why it earns the value title.

Choose it if you want one machine for most kitchen work. The caveat is that it is still a large bowl, so very small portions process less cleanly.
products.idealFor: Home cooks wanting one capable all-rounder.

products.name: Breville BFP610 Sous Chef 9 Cup Food Processor
products.verdict: A 9-cup stainless Sous Chef that suits everyday cooking without hogging counter space.
products.description:
The Breville BFP610 Sous Chef has a 9-cup bowl and brushed stainless steel construction from the Sous Chef line. It keeps the build quality of the BFP810 in a body sized for daily use.

It ranks below the Cuisinart DFP-14BCNY because the bowl is smaller and the listing shows fewer named functions. You gain a tidier footprint and a metal feel, and give up capacity.

Pick it for a two to four person household. The caveat is that large doughs and shredding for a party need several rounds.
products.idealFor: Small households that still want stainless build quality.
products.skipIf: You regularly cook for large groups.

products.name: Cuisinart Pro Custom 11-Cup Food Processor, DLC-8SBCYP1
products.verdict: An 11-cup machine with dishwasher-safe parts and slicing and shredding discs included.
products.description:
The Cuisinart Pro Custom 11-Cup has an 11-cup bowl, dishwasher-safe parts and slicing and shredding discs in the box. The dishwasher listing is the standout, since cleanup is where food processors lose people.

It ranks under the Breville BFP610 because it offers a little more bowl but less of the premium metal finish. You get convenience instead of luxury.

It fits busy weeknight cooks. The caveat is that the listing is thinner on motor detail than the DFP-14 models, so check the wattage before you buy.
products.skipIf: You want a stainless premium feel.

products.name: Breville BFP638 Paradice 9 Processor and Dicer
products.verdict: A 9-cup stainless processor with a dedicated dicing function.
products.description:
The Breville BFP638 Paradice 9 is a 9-cup brushed stainless processor with a dedicated dicing function. Even cubes for salsa or mirepoix are the thing most standard discs struggle with.

It ranks below the Pro Custom because it costs more for a smaller bowl, and the value is in that single dicing feature. You trade capacity and easy cleanup for precision.

Choose it if you dice often. The caveat is that if you rarely cut cubes, the dicer is a feature you pay for and ignore.
products.idealFor: Cooks who dice onions and veg weekly.

products.name: Cuisinart FP-130 13-Cup Multifunctional Food Processor
products.verdict: A 13-cup multifunctional processor for cooks who want capacity without extras.
products.description:
The Cuisinart FP-130 offers a 13-cup bowl and multifunctional processing modes. The listing is short on specifics, which is its main weakness next to better documented rivals.

It ranks last because it lacks the named motor power, dicing or discs detail that justify the other picks. You get decent capacity and a familiar brand.

It works if you want a plain 13-cup option. The caveat is that you should confirm what attachments ship with it before ordering.
products.idealFor: Shoppers wanting a simple large-bowl machine.

methodology.description: Dishwasher-safe parts and footprint count for daily use.

whatMatters.detail: Bowl size is measured in cups of working capacity, and it sets how much you can process at once. Too big and small jobs spread thin on the blade; too small and big jobs need rounds. Match it to your usual batch, and check the cup figure in the product title.

Wattage tells you how well the machine handles dense dough and hard vegetables. A 720-watt motor like the DFP-14BCNY copes with dough, while an unlisted wattage is a question mark. Look for the number in the bullets rather than a vague power claim.

Most food processors chop and shred but turn dicing into mush. A dedicated dicing function, as on the Paradice 9, produces even cubes. Check the listing for the word dicing and an included dicing kit.

Parts that fit in a dishwasher save real effort, and sharp discs are the hardest part to hand wash. Check the listing for dishwasher-safe wording, and note how many pieces you must clean after each use.
A large processor needs counter or cabinet space, and many get left in boxes. Compare height and base size with where it will live. A 9-cup unit is easier to keep out than a 16-cup one.

faq.q: Is a bigger food processor always better?
faq.a: No. Oversized bowls spread small amounts thin and take more storage. Match capacity to your normal batch.

faq.q: What is the most common buying mistake?
faq.a: Paying for cup size you never use. Most households do well with 9 to 14 cups.

faq.q: Is the Breville worth it over the Cuisinart?
faq.a: It is if you value brushed stainless build or a dicing function. The Cuisinart DFP-14BCNY matches core tasks for less.
The Cuisinart DFP-14 models list dough among their functions. Check each listing for dough mentions before relying on it.

faq.q: How should I clean the discs?
faq.a: Wash the blades carefully, away from your hands. Dishwasher-safe parts, as on the Pro Custom, help.

faq.q: Why did you leave out the Ninja?
faq.a: The Ninja BlendSense is a 72 oz blender system, not a true food processor, so it does not match this ranking.

finalTake: The Breville BFP810 is the best food processor under $500 if you cook big, and the Cuisinart DFP-14BCNY is the smarter buy for most kitchens. Choose the BFP610 for small households and the Pro Custom if cleanup decides it. Match bowl size to your real batches and you will be happy.
